ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left is quadrilateral ABCD, side AB is labeled x+1, and side CD is labeled x-1; on the right is quadrilateral EFGH, side EF is labeled 8, and side GH is labeled 5. Angle markings show that the corresponding vertices are A to E, B to F, C to G, and D to H, so corresponding sides are AB to EF and CD to GH. Reasoning: Since the two polygons are similar, corresponding sides are proportional, so (x+1)/8 = (x-1)/5. Cross-multiplying gives 5(x+1)=8(x-1), that is, 5x+5=8x-8, so 13=3x, x=13/3. CD is required, and CD=x-1, so CD=13/3-1=10/3.

method.method_draft: Read the angle markings in the image to match corresponding vertices of the similar quadrilaterals: A matches E, B matches F, C matches G, and D matches H. Therefore side AB on the smaller polygon corresponds to EF on the larger polygon, and side CD corresponds to GH. From the image, AB is labeled x+1, CD is labeled x-1, EF is 8, and GH is 5. Use proportional corresponding sides: (x+1)/8 = (x-1)/5, or equivalently (x+1)/(x-1)=8/5. Solve 5(x+1)=8(x-1), giving x=13/3, then CD=x-1=10/3.
